images.title: A trip in four steps
images.purpose: Show a journey problem as steps along a road: start, spend, get, spend, and the money left.
images.composition: A road with four stops, the amounts and the operations at each step, and the money left.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. A road with four stops and the money of one trip. A thick road line in grey #6B7280 (10 px) runs horizontally at y 420 from x 120 to x 1336, with 4 round stops (circle 44 px diameter, filled amber #E69F00, outlined dark #2B2B2B 3 px) at x 180, 520, 860 and 1200. Above each stop, centred on it, a rounded label card (280 by 110 px, y 250 to 360, outlined teal #0072B2 4 px) with text in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (40 px): Start ₹15,000 (first), Spends ₹4,250 (second), Gets ₹2,000 (third) and Spends ₹3,160 (fourth). Below each of the last three stops, centred on it, y 490, one operation tag in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (56 px): − 4,250, + 2,000 and − 3,160. At the bottom, centred at x 728, y 680, a rounded badge outlined green #009E73 (5 px), x 428 to 1028, y 620 to 740, with the text Left ₹9,590 in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (72 px). At the bottom right, x 1230, y 770, the small caption practice values in construction grey #6B7280 bold sans-serif (32 px). No other text. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
an operation sign that does not match its step
images.takeaway: Read the story one step at a time: take away when money is spent, add when money is given.
images.description: A road with the steps Start ₹15,000, Spends ₹4,250, Gets ₹2,000, Spends ₹3,160 and the result Left ₹9,590.
images.context: Concept image for Journey Problems: Add or Subtract, Then Estimate, Section A, using the example's own numbers (practice values). The book's own route and amounts stay on the question cards.
images.teaching_notes: Say take away or add at each stop. The slip to watch: adding when the money is spent.

images.title: Round up, add, compare
images.purpose: Show an estimate: each price rounded up to the next thousand, added, and compared with the money to spend.
images.composition: Three amounts with their rounded-up values, the rounded total 45,000 and the comparison with 50,000.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. Three amounts each rounded up, and the check against the money to spend. Three rows. Each row has a LEFT BOX (x 150 to 600, 450 by 100 px, filled amber #E69F00, outlined dark #2B2B2B 3 px) with the real amount, a thick dark arrow (6 px) from x 620 to x 820, and a RIGHT BOX (x 840 to 1290, 450 by 100 px, filled teal #0072B2, outlined dark 3 px) with the rounded amount, all text in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (64 px). Row 1 y 110 to 210: ₹19,820 and ₹20,000. Row 2 y 240 to 340: ₹14,480 and ₹15,000. Row 3 y 370 to 470: ₹9,765 and ₹10,000. Below, a green #009E73 outlined rounded banner (x 250 to 1206, y 530 to 620, 5 px) with the line 20,000 + 15,000 + 10,000 = 45,000 in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (56 px), and under it, centred at x 728, y 700, the line 45,000 is less than 50,000 in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (56 px). At the bottom right, x 1230, y 770, the small caption practice values in construction grey #6B7280 bold sans-serif (32 px). No other text. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a rounded amount that is not the next thousand up
the exact total 44,065 anywhere in the frame (it belongs to the check, not the estimate)
images.takeaway: Round each price up, add, and compare: 45,000 is less than 50,000, so the money is enough.
images.description: Three prices rounded up to 20,000, 15,000 and 10,000, their total 45,000 and the comparison 45,000 is less than 50,000.
images.context: Concept image for Journey Problems: Add or Subtract, Then Estimate, Section B, using the example's own numbers (practice values).
images.teaching_notes: Say why the real total is less than the rounded one: each price was rounded up. The slip to watch: expecting the estimate to be exact.

image_decisions.why: One video, two sections, one picture each: the road with its steps shows how the operations follow the story in Section A, and the rounded amounts beside the real amounts make the estimate visible in Section B.
